landmarks.name: Cidade Velha
landmarks.writeup: A historic town and UNESCO World Heritage site, known as the oldest settlement in Cape Verde and a former Portuguese colonial capital.

landmarks.name: Fogo Volcano
landmarks.writeup: An active volcano on Fogo Island, offering hiking opportunities and unique volcanic landscapes.

landmarks.name: Sal Island Beaches
landmarks.writeup: Famous for white sandy beaches and clear waters, popular for tourism and water sports.

landmarks.name: Praia
landmarks.writeup: The capital city, known for its cultural sites, markets, and vibrant urban life.

landmarks.name: Monte Verde
landmarks.writeup: The highest peak in Cape Verde, located on São Vicente Island, offering panoramic views.

cultural_events.name: Carnival of Mindelo
cultural_events.writeup: A colorful and lively carnival celebrated on São Vicente Island, featuring music, dance, and parades.

cultural_events.name: Baía das Gatas Music Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual music festival held on São Vicente Island, attracting local and international artists.

cultural_events.name: Festival de Grogue
cultural_events.writeup: A festival celebrating grogue, a traditional Cape Verdean sugarcane liquor.

food_writeup: Cape Verdean cuisine blends African, Portuguese, and Brazilian influences, featuring dishes like cachupa (a slow-cooked stew of corn, beans, and fish or meat), fresh seafood, and tropical fruits.
brief_history: Cape Verde was uninhabited until discovered and colonized by the Portuguese in the 15th century. It became an important center for the transatlantic slave trade. The country gained independence from Portugal in 1975 and has since developed a stable democratic government.

important_people.name: Cesária Évora
important_people.description: Renowned singer known as the 'Barefoot Diva'

current_conflicts: Cape Verde is currently peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts.
